match.reason: Neither bank point teaches how exchange rate, terms of trade and competitiveness changes affect the macroeconomic goals and living standards; the exchange rate card covers only business-level price effects on exporters and importers, and the goal setting card is about business decisions.

draft.title: Effects on goals and living standards
card: A lower Australian dollar makes exports cheaper overseas and imports dearer here. Exports tend to rise and imports tend to fall, which lifts demand for Australian output. This can support economic growth and jobs.

Dearer imports raise the prices of imported goods and of inputs such as fuel and machinery. This tends to push up inflation. A higher dollar has the opposite effects: cheaper imports and lower inflation, but weaker exports and fewer jobs in trade-exposed industries.
A rise in the terms of trade means exports buy more imports. It tends to raise national income and spending, and it often lifts the dollar too. A fall does the reverse.

Better competitiveness raises export sales and cuts import demand, which helps growth and jobs. These changes shift the economic goals, and so living standards, but the size of the effect depends on other factors.
draft.remember: A lower dollar tends to help exports, growth and jobs but add to inflation. A higher dollar tends to do the reverse.

a.q: The Australian dollar depreciates. What is the most likely effect on the economy?
opts: Exports rise and import prices rise
Exports fall and import prices rise
Exports rise and import prices fall
Exports fall and import prices fall
a.why: A lower dollar makes Australian exports cheaper overseas, so they tend to rise. It makes imports dearer in Australia. The other options mix up which way each side moves.
a.clue: What happens to the price of exports in foreign currency?

b.q: Australia's terms of trade rise strongly, and the dollar appreciates. Which effect on a tourism exporter and on inflation is most likely?
opts: Exports weaken, and import prices fall, easing inflation
Exports rise, and import prices rise, adding to inflation
Exports weaken, and import prices rise, adding to inflation
Exports rise, and import prices fall, easing inflation
b.why: A higher dollar makes Australian goods and services dearer to foreigners, so exports such as tourism weaken. It also makes imports cheaper, which eases inflation. The higher terms of trade lift income, but the dollar effect on this exporter is negative.
b.clue: Does a higher dollar make Australia dearer or cheaper for visitors?

a.best: Exports rise and import prices rise

b.best: Exports weaken, and import prices fall, easing inflation
